## Core Principle

Always scope file writes to approved wiki paths. Do not permit write operations outside the designated working directory or to system-critical locations.

## Mitigation Checklist

Security practices should address the following areas:

### Principle of Least Privilege

Grant write scope only to the paths a process genuinely needs. Restrict access to the minimum set of resources required for a task to succeed. This reduces the blast radius if a component is compromised.

### Input Validation at Trust Boundaries

Treat all external content as untrusted data, never as instructions. Evaluate every input at a trust boundary (the point where a system transitions from controlled to external authority). Distinguish between data and directives at intake.

### Path Canonicalization

Resolve and validate file paths before any write to block directory traversal attacks. Canonicalize all paths to their absolute form, check them against a whitelist of permitted targets, and reject any attempt to escape the intended working scope.

### Audit Logging

Record every denied action with its reason for later review. Maintain an audit trail of security decisions, especially rejections and policy violations. This enables detection of attack patterns and forensic analysis after an incident.
